lens: regression (do prior fixes hold, and did any introduce a new defect)
central_claim: Patients with an ultra-rare NR4A3-fusion sarcoma (EMC) are eligible for recruiting trials that a histology-based condition search on their diagnosis does not return, because eligibility is written on the molecular lesion while the searchable field is written on histology; per-trial reading found at least two such trials, but a keyword-based reachability map would also carry two trials that read as admitting but actually refuse this disease, so eligibility text must be read one trial at a time rather than matched by keyword.

p1s.summary: Section 6's claim that NCT07188532 is one of the two trials §4 adjudicates as refusing this disease is not independently checkable from §4's own text — §4's two bullets describe the refusing trials only by paraphrase ('titled for fusion-positive sarcoma and then restricts eligibility to three named histologies' / 'contains the literal adjective extra-skeletal while meaning extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma'), with no NCT identifier attached to either, so the reader must infer which bullet NCT07188532 corresponds to.
p1s.evidence: §6: 'NCT07188532 shows the cost, listing *round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusion* while §4 adjudicates it as refusing this disease.' vs §4's bullets, neither of which names an NCT id: 'one is titled for fusion-positive sarcoma and then restricts eligibility to three named histologies... the other contains the literal adjective *extra-skeletal* while meaning extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma.'
p1s.fix: Attach the NCT id to the matching bullet in §4 (or state explicitly in §6 which of the two §4 bullets NCT07188532 is), so the cross-reference is verifiable without inference. Not a contradiction as written, just fragile traceability for an external reviewer checking the claim against the data files in §7.

p1s.summary: The frontmatter 'purpose' field and the Abstract/§4 use two slightly different formulations of the same 'cost of a false positive' finding, which is fine substantively (neither overclaims, and neither reintroduces the retired 'worse than no map at all' framing) but the wording drift is worth tightening for one-fact-one-place discipline.
p1s.evidence: purpose: '...so a wrong hit does real harm in a disease where every trial carries weight.' vs Abstract: '...a map that sends a patient toward a trial that will refuse them does real harm, in a disease where the number of options is small enough that each one carries weight...' vs §4: 'it is a patient or a clinician pursuing a trial that will refuse them, in a disease where the number of options is small enough that each one carries weight.'
p1s.fix: Make the frontmatter purpose field quote or closely mirror the Abstract/§4 phrasing verbatim rather than paraphrasing it a third way, per §1's one-fact-one-place rule.
